Don't get me wrong, Going to PCs for a second, a GeForce 1080 Ti is noticeably better than a 970 ... but the 970 from three years ago is still pretty damn good. You'll notice the different, but overall game-play believably isn't really impacted that much. (A 970M can still play the first Tomb Raider reboot in 4k, and Rise of the Tomb Raider in 2k).

Both Sony and Microsoft want the real next gen: super realistic graphics hardware. Like, uncanny valley level graphics .. and I think we will get there, but it is a bit away for both nVidia and AMD.

The other big thing that's missing: 120Hz UHD. Right not most PC gamers have gone back to ultra-wide regular HD monitors because the higher refresh rate it worth way more than 4k resolution. For fast paced games, it affects game play in multi-player.

Right now if you want 120Hz from a home console to a TV, you're going to need special TVs and multiple HDMI or DisplayPorts. I think HDMI 2.0a is still limited to 60HZ (although it allows 10-bit). We're going to need the next HDMI standard before we can do 120Hz between consoles and TVs. Even for PC gamers, there are very few 120Hz/4k setups and they often involve SLI cards and super expensive monitors.
